view.inverse: lon = degrees(x/scale + radians(lon_min)); lat = degrees(2.5*(atan(exp(0.8*(y_top - y/scale))) - pi/4))
view.units: canvas px, origin top-left, y down; integers
view.orientation: rings clockwise on screen: sum(x_i*y_(i+1) - x_(i+1)*y_i) > 0
view.x_wrap_note: x + width is the same meridian; draw routes that cross the 180th meridian twice (at x and x +/- width)

ice_note: Antarctic ice shelves (Natural Earth ice-shelf polygons); draw under land
notes: Twenty Thousand Leagues branch. Miller cylindrical, centred on Greenwich; x wraps at the 180th meridian.
Antarctica land = grounding line; ice shelves are in "ice". The Aral Sea is a hand-drawn historical approximation; modern reservoirs removed.
Small story islands are exaggerated in "islets" (scale > 1); New Elba and Lincoln Island are fictional blobs.
